content:
And she makes her third and (hopefully) final deal with the ravens. Irynx Berlio walks out of Kingsbridge that day with a little bundle of a girl: Corbianne Berlio Lundsdóttir, the daughter of the grove. Knowing they'd leave one day, Irynx hopes that Cor will treasure these memories of Empire City when she grows up, of running around Murry Hill with Kukudh and Orphy, climbing the roots of Cael'fii, and helping count all the ball bearings in the Ordinary. 

The day comes when the work is done, and there's nothing left to do in Empire City. Irynx finds there are some things she'd like to leave behind after all. She leaves the Raven Queen to the Speaker for the Dead, and hopes it will become a home for him rather than just a warship. 

She packs more supplies than necessary for the journey, Irynx believes in being prepared. They have a going-away party, because of course they have to have a going away party, and then it's time for goodbye. Her daughter in one arm, and the mothman egg in another, her tale in Empire City ends. 

So begins <#880280609170264084>.

content:
As the years began to blur by, Bo begins to lose all sense of time. He has no idea how many years he has been ferrying the dead, but one day... 

Lucy beams with excitement... 

Another Bo has seen before is about to ride, Lucy tells him. He ponders a moment, trying to guess who it could be before he shrugs and grabs his banjo, ready to ease the travel for whomever is joining him. The light grows brightly from lucy as she takes her post on the carpet, she begins giggling. 

A bright flash of light herolds the way... But... Something is off...

 Something, Bo hasnt quite fully expected. He is joined by two souls this time..."uh... This is new...." Another light beams from above..."t-three? All at once?!?!" As the light fades, the three souls sit formless in front of him, much like wisps.

Bo sits, blinking curiously. "Um... Uh... Hiya you three... " bo smiles warmly as he haphazardly waves, still confused. "Now then... Lets see your story shall we?" He asks as he bows graciously. As lucy flies around... She tilts her head as, something off-sets her. 

Before bo could start his normal ritual of playing his mother's lullaby... A song begins to echo from 2 of the 3 wisps. Lucy quickly moves in, and boops one of the wisps. Bo looks on, confused as the wisp takes form, and his ears twitch to the melody the goblin before him is singing. As Lucy boops the next wisp, the remaining 2 wisps take form. A Goblin in armor, and a small puppy... The song becomes shockingky clear to Bo now. The two goblins before him... Are singing his mother's lullaby. He quickly adds to the melody andnsings along, much to the suprise of Rockman and Leaf. It takes a moment for bo to recognize one of the goblins, before he begins to be licked by a small puppy. It is indeed a very small dog, but his bark echoes through the realm Bo travels in.

thread.name: Bos epilogue

content:
Bo pets the puppy only briefly, before a memory flashes in his head, the oasis. "HEY! ..... Ain't you... Gil's friend?" Bo asks. The male goblin gives bo a thumbs up and smiles.
"Yeap! You were there in Gil's oasis the day he appeared, weren't ya?" Lucy beams in, and in an instant, he witnesses the life story of the 3... Of Rockman, Leaf, and Rush. 

Bo's eyes grow wide with excitement as he see's Sandigil, the coins passed around for his mayoral candidacy. He's excited to watch....up until bo himself see's the horrors in town square, Sandigil's head on a pike. The fight with the Hunger... And the wish rockman had made... To wish Sandigil back to life. He quickly moves over and shakes Rickman's hand, as Leaf steps forward and asks how it was that Bo knew their song. 

Dormant memories flood Bo's mind, of being a smol bun. He had scrapped his knee... And his mother begain singing. 
"Mama, where'd you learn that song?" Bo asked.
All she responded with, was a smile as he kept singing.

"My mother sang it to me... Later on she finally told me, that lullaby had been passed down for generations." Bo chuckkes. Rockman and Leaf both look towards each other and smile, holding hands.

Meanwhile, the puppy Rush flies around chasing a panicking Lucy. Voices echo from the two as they spin around in the air.
"play? Play? Play?" -rush
"Aaaaaah he's so slobery!" -lucy

Bo, Rockman, and Leaf all laugh together as the carpet, at first unknowingly to Bo, slowly rises up. Higher and higher as a light beams down from the sky above.

As they sit and talk, Bo eventually notices the change in scenery. As golden light fills the area, a small fish flies down, spinning around Leaf. Leaf's face beams with joy as Rush and Lucy fly over. The trio ascend up even higher as Rockman and Leaf begins to phase back into living boddies. Bo looks on in amazement as the puppy grows and his bark begins to deepen. 

"Mello!" Rockman and Leaf both cheer in ecitement as they both move in to hug the fish. In another flash, the fish transformed into that of a young woman. Bo smiles and sits back, letting the three float up. 

Bo exchanges waves with the trio as they fade away with Mello. As the carpet descends back to the River, bo smiles. Lucy beams down and nuzzles bo before they resume their journey along the river.

On the banks near by, a form fades as they smile up to the sky. Web sighs as their voice echoes.

"Truly goodbye this time. Take good care, Mello. Take good care." -Web.

content:
**The End…** *or the beginning?*

Malathor remains in Empire city for another six months, in this time he teaches Nolan everything he knows of the still developing field of medicine. He spends several evenings teaching Secel various rituals and clever tricks to avoid future attempts at possession by powerful otherworldly entities. Malathor keeps his word, awarding the titles of Pitar Raxacoricofallapatorius, and Vorbitor Finn Midask, to Rax and Finn should they choose to accept them. 

Malathor will leave ownership and management of his workshop to Jigsaw to do with it as they please, and spends his last night in this place that has been his home, walking through the city, occasionally scattering a handful of appleseeds along the green grasses and bare dirt.


Malathor stands on the deck of an airship bound to Europe. He looks out over the city with a smile.
“All has gone according to plan, the foundations have been laid…”
***Thunder Rumbles in the distance. There is a storm coming.***

*The Banderhobb stands on a rooftop, watching the ship sailing away though the clouds until it disappears from sight. It croaks once, leaps down into a narrow alleyway, and then melds into the shadows.*
(And for those that dont know the song....)

content: Thank you

So this is not an IC epilogue, but more of my way of thanking you all as my way of wrapping up the season.  I won’t speak for other DMs, but my journey this season really did start last season.  Thank you all for letting me say goodbye to my favorite character.  And thank you all for saying goodbye.  He’s now part of the official lore of Arcania, but in my mind Gil’s story is over.  He will appear in the future, but only as the other wardens do, both a part of the world, and not a part of the game, touching where they need to, but not super active presence.

I set out this season to give anyone who needs it closure with him, but in the end, I got the closure I needed.  So again, thank you for that.

Beyond that, I got to write so much content for the creepy oppressive section of town.  I was so excited to see Crane breathe life into it, and other DMs take time to run things there.  It was a blast to see you all deal with the horrors that were in every nook and cranny of Hampstead.  Every time you all had an event there, I had trouble sleeping, so excited to find out the next day how it went.  And man, you all went above and beyond what I could have hoped.  So again, thank you.  I don’t think I would have made it through the season without the players seeming so encouraged by the content I wrote.

We all went through a lot this season, just as we did last season, but most importantly, we have all expanded the community, and created new friendships.  Anyway, I want to thank you all for giving life to the world we built.  Without the players, there really would be no game, and no reason for the DMs to plan.  I’ll see you all on the Tales server, I am sure.  It’ll go quiet from time to time, but know, we will be working on S5, with the same love and care we gave S4.

Love,
Heki AKA Sandigil

content: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

**Eliot:** 
After spending a bit further time with Jigsaw, Raxacoricofallapatorius, and Mike, Eloise excuses herself to return to the Crepes and Crits Café, meeting with Willow outside to have another heavy conversation along with collecting some personal belongings,  Before returning to Cael'fii and Demetrius.

With the king dead, the war over, and the city and nation uniting, things seem to be settling down, as settle as a major metropolis can be under such conditions. Eloise takes a few hours each day to begin teaching Sabrine Arcanian Sign Language, (at no cost) which Roy and Kukudh are welcome to participate in. She aids in rebuilding the park in New Hempstead using a few uses of Plant Growth. 

As everything settles down and Eloise has more time to sort out her thoughts and feelings she asks those closest to her to refer to them as El, and while they still didn't quite feel like themselves they felt better than before.

El says goodbye to the part of themselves that was Eloise one week after their death and rebirth. They are glad to have had the opportunity to form the happy memories they did and  come to peace with who they were once upon a time, but it is not who they are.

After informing Demetrius of where El was at, in regards to finding themselves, El begins to grow more secretive and recluse. Not out of any wrongdoing or deteriorating mental state, simply the impending deadline of the pact made. The deadline and responsibility weigh on El as if they were carrying the whole cafe and the foundation of which it stood upon their back. 

On September 6th, 1776 two days prior to the deadline El presents a masterful blend of tea to Demetrius, beaming with pride, glad to finally have kept their part of their deal. However, it was still lacking something and it was not enough to leave Demetrius speechless nor was it the perfect blend. Shattered, heartbroken and defeated, realizing that no matter how much effort they put in within the next two days it would not be enough. The months they had spent afraid of the outside finally taking its toll. Through tears El pledged their eternal service to Demetrius until they were able to get it right.
-

thread.name: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
Shortly following this pledge, El put Willow in charge of the cafe until the debt was paid off. They donned their tailcoat and accompanied Demetrius most places, when allowed, and offered their services where applicable as a butler. Secretly El was happy to spend as much time as they could in Demetrius' company, and it was a secret not well hidden from the other court members of Feyrytown. But El kept their demeanor professional regardless of who Demetrius was meeting with and always had tea on hand. On the extraordinarily rare occurrence where meetings took a darker turn, El also performed the duties of a bodyguard. Not that the ancient fey needed the help, but as a way to help insure neither resorted to their violent pasts. 
Six months after their death, El returns to being Eliot, once more comfortable in who he is. Eliot dyes his hair back to his well known mint color, but there is a single streak of gold along the left side. Three years of companionship and servitude to Demetrius pass before they are granted passage, for a singular day, to where Demetrius' home once was. Upon seeing the beauty, Eliot understood what his tea had been missing. He separates himself from Demetrius for a short time to gather some flowers and a bit of the soil. Saving them for a later surprise.

On the anniversary of their fifth year together Eliot invites Demitrius on a surprise trip for their anniversary, Eliot is shy but proud to show Demetrius the Demiplane he had crafted for the couple to share, a replica of Demetrius’ home. It wasn’t quite perfect, but it was enough for the two of them to call their own home.
-

thread.name: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
Years pass, and Eliot grows older yet Demitrius remains the same. Eliot has a longing to be part of Demitrius’ life for as long as the fey had already lived. But knows he can’t, instead he looks into something originally only a fleeting desire from his youth, and came back to him briefly in the presence of a certain radiant familiar. Eliot looks into dragons and their kin. A child the couple could raise together, and not be bound by Eliot’s own mortality. He didn’t want Demetris to grieve his passing, or worsen it by a child of theirs also passing long before the archfey’s time was up.

It took several more years before Eliot was able to get an egg with help from Prosser stopping some smugglers. Then presenting it to Demetrius, a large egg coated in deep red scales. Despite the off color Eliot consider’s Trapero as a name for the dragon, but discusses it with Prosser first. They mention that if it were to be named in Trapero’s honor they’d prefer it to be Prospero, the name the twins held before they were split.  

Soon after receiving the egg the small red dragon is running amok and driving Eliot up walls just to keep up with the wild child and its flames. Despite all the stress a smile never leaves his face, particularly when seeing young Prospero and Demetrius bonding while Eliot cleans scorch marks and regrows flowers.

Many uneventful years pass, and Eliot enjoys the chaotic peace with his small family. But he knows his life is drawing near. Many other humans he’s known of his years have passed, and he’s seen waves upon wave’s of Sutri’s own children become adults in their own right, and even see some of them move on to whatever happened next. He takes Demetrius out one one more date, to the small little cafe that began it all, and brews up a pot of tea for them both. A special recipe he had figured out oh so many years ago, on the trip to Demitrius’ home. A recipe he didn’t need to be confident in, a recipe he knew was the one. He sat across from Demitrius and acted as if there was nothing special about the tea by taking the first sip, before relishing the look on his partner’s face and making a gentle comment that he finally paid of his debt for fulfilling his childhood dream, and being thankful to have helped make so many other people’s dreams come true, including his own, all at the side of the most wonderful partner.
-

thread.name: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content: Eliot passes away in his sleep two weeks later on August 24, 1846. Exactly seventy years after The Whispering Wolf killed him, at the age of 97. Leaving behind Demetrius, their 53 year old child, and the cafe. His will does not contain much, as he never had much. He does leave behind a very precious tea pot, inside on a very worn and folded piece of paper is the recipe for the perfect tea, which he leaves to Demetrius. And the intricate silver timepiece he leaves for Prospero as a memento.

thread.name: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
**Willow:**
Willow learned Eliot's lessons with a great interest and took his plans for the café and built upon it. She continued to run the café, although the hours fluctuated for a time as there was no longer a manager that didn't sleep, many of the regular cliental understood however and gave the café the opportunity it needed to grow from where Eliot had started. Willow allowed stray animals to continue to come, go and  volunteer, however she was noticeably more determined to have a working staff over volunteers to provide a better service to the customers of the café. 

True to her words with Demetrius and Ferrah, she helped couch other animals through the process and eventual awakening of those under her employ. Not all took her up on the offer which she understood, it was a lot to process and even a few years after her own awakening found it a lot to deal with and missed simpler times.

On multiple occasions, larger businesses attempted to buy out the café, only to have their attempts thwarted and offers returned in shreds. Leaving them to settle for cheap knock offs of the critter exclusively operated café, such as Starpaws or Cheesy Chucks, which were only humanoids in animal costume.

One side effect that she had *not* been prepared for due to her Awakening was an extended life span compared to what she would have normally expected.  She owned and operated the cafe the remainder of her days. Willow passes on in her sleep June 23, 1821 at the age of 53.

thread.name: The Epilogue of a Certain Café

content:
The war is over but the world still moves on. Life at Empire City slowly but surely gets back on track. First order of business; rebuilding Hampstead. The speaker didn’t spend too much time here but a project such as rebuilding an entire borough would need all the help it can get. Amidst the rebuilding, the Speaker tries to pay as much homage and respect to the dead as he can.

    Amidst all the busywork, the Speaker manages to hangout with his friends in the city. He meditates in Murry Hill Park and helps with the Mender and Sabrine. He debates with Vivica Midask about philosophy and politics. And he reconnects with his first friend, Irynx. It was a long and arduous adventure to get to where they were now. Things between them will never be the same and that’s good. The Speaker has grown and matured and his relationships reflect this. Once naive and lost now wisened and hardened by loss.

    Irynx leaves their Airship, now christened as the Raven Queen, under the Speaker’s care. Ace Pilot Wings heavy in his pocket, the Speaker agrees gladly. He gives away his old airship and moves into the Queen. While remodeling and rearranging, the Speaker comes across a fairly surprising discovery. In a small crack by the airship walls lies an extradimensional captain’s quarters with none other but Meorys inside. Meorys was using some Nolzur’s Marvelous Pigments to counterfeit some coin, both continental currency and British pounds and stockpiling them in a box labeled ‘Just in case the revolution fails’. In her paranoia, Meorys has missed the revolution.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
The Speaker bids farewell to all of his friends at the city and embarks on his first trip out of Arcania borders. He journeys south for Meorys’s hometown to drop her off there. Meorys tells the Speaker that they both came from here and that the Speaker was once a noble of this lands, the Faranells she said. The Speaker has no memories of this whatsoever but one this is for sure, the person that left this place for Empire city is no longer. That person died long ago and now the Speaker, a brand new person, stands in their place. Meorys and the Speaker bid each other farewell, marking the end to the Ball Eater crew.

    The Speaker embarks on his next adventure. Time to finish up his deal with a dragon. He lays out his tarot deck in front of him, the world card face up serving to strengthen his connection to the spirit world as he calls out for Nidhogg. Invoking the name of Nidhogg with the intention to speak with him gives the Speaker the feeling of his cold breath wrapping around your skin. A low growl rumbles against his chest, the dragon of Yggdrasil is listening.

The Speaker takes a deep breath to collect his thoughts. "The war against Britain is over, Arcania has won. Though I assume you already know this. I am here to hold up my end of the bargain. I am awaiting your orders." The Speaker speaks with forced politeness. "Cross you the eastern Ocean. Bring yourself to bear against my enemies, Ephemeral." The Speaker grins mentally. "Nice timing, I was about to go there myself." He then scolds himself as he regains seriousness. "Enemies? Odin?"

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
"The Aesir move against the once and future king. My people enslaved by the Hanging one, the one eyed God of Thieves and Heroes is bringing the berzerker rage against the Knights of the Round. The war is pitched and laying waste to all of the lands between them. Gods who call themselves good ignore the Gods who call themselves evil to make war against one another. And in the midst of these battles, Arthur's Dragon Merlin moves against my people. My servants among the living."

"And this is where I step in." The Speaker lets out a breath of relief. He was bracing himself for Nidhogg ordering him to do unspeakable atrocities, continuing the fight against Britain is no such thing. "Who am I fighting with? Is there a representative of your people I am to meet up with?"

"Saint George the Dragon Slayer is named among the great heroes of Britannia. Morgana Le fey would see Merlin destroyed. Aid her in this and then she shall aid you in the defeat of Saint George. Without his dragon lance, my people: the trolls, the dark elves, the giants shall no longer fear that Jörmungandr be slain."

The Speaker nods. "I understand. I will head out for Britain, seek out these people, and defeat the king's dragon. I shall do this to uphold our agreement and to help your people. Evil, good, or anything else I shall not let anyone be oppressed by the British no longer. I'll be meeting you once more after this is all over, in one way or another."

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
"You will not meet me again. You are my unshackling. You have bound yourself to my service. And that service extends into your death. At the time of your death, I will finally abdicate Hel and name you my successor. Foolish mortal. Your death will be an unending task of tending to the unwanted dead."

The Speaker flinches and nearly falls to the ground. This is the catch he's been expecting, but in all his wildest imaginations, this wasn't in them. He is speechless.

Nidhogg fades. His command is complete.

He remembers all he's been through to put him in this situation and regains his composure. He starts speaking to no one in particular. "As Speaker for the Dead, I accept this." Not like he had a choice. "Unwanted the souls under me may be, but voiceless they will not. I shall serve as a warning for those who unnecessarily give away parts of themselves. Those who purposely throw away themselves shall end up under the watch of the Nameless Speaker." 

With a heavy heart, the speaker sails for Britain.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
Before anything else, the Speaker first assembles a crew. A ship needs more than just a pilot, especially when fighting a dragon. The Speaker rounds up those not loyal to the crown, those who have a bone to settle with the monarchy. The frivolous behavior of the former King George saw to the Speaker seeing no shortage of able helpers. He calls on the help of a young inventor, a kenku priestess of a god of trickery, a shady gunslinger, a loxodon folk singer, and brutish barbarian. With a ramshackle crew under his command, the Speaker flies for Morgana Le Fey, sworn enemy to the dragon Merlin.

    Finding Morgana was easy enough, she wasn’t exactly subtle with her actions. Convincing her to join was the hard part. Morgana is a powerful sorceress, as stubborn as she is talented. She believed that no one was worthy to be deemed on her level and only she alone can take on the challenge of fighting Merlin. Fortunately, playing the role of one below another is something the Speaker is highly familiar with. With some clever words and silvered promises of a ship, Morgana Le Fey joins the crew of the Raven Queen. She grows tired of working in dingy castles and dungeons, a flying base of operations would be a much better replacement.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
With his crew now assembled and a powerful sorceress at his side. Merlin’s time is coming to an end. The Raven Queen flies south, it flies for Wales.

    Without Morgana’s long accrued knowledge of Merlin and its weaknesses, the Speaker wouldn’t be able to take out the dragon and without the Speaker and his crew Morgana would’ve lacked the needed firepower and resilience to outmatch Merlin. It is only through their cooperation that Merin would fall. Through the help of the spirits and the brute strength of the nordic dead, Merlin is flushed out of his lair. Morgana’s magicks keep him distracted and bogged down while the artillery fire of the Raven Queen tears away at his defenses. Taking a page out of Captain Midask’s book on how to slay a dragon the Speaker constructs a volatile creation using the leftovers of Meorys’s pigments, tempered with the expertise of the mechanic onboard. With this ramshackle contraption of oil flasks and ball bearings, Merlin is laid to rest. The wings of Arthur fall and the forces of Odin descend upon the British isles. The speaker’s job isn’t over yet however, there is still one foe that stands between him and his duty. Saint George the Dragonslayer needs to be cast down.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
The fight with Merlin renders the Raven Queen grounded and its crew busy. The Speaker and Morgana alone face the saint. This battle plays out differently from the clash with Merlin. Without his ship around them, the Speaker and Morgana are vulnerable and Saint George proves to be a highly competent combatant. It is only through sheer luck and with the strength of spirits, quite literally, that the Speaker continues to fight. With berserkers surrounding him and Morgana’s magic manipulating the tides of the battle, Saint George is almost beaten, but his aim proves true and his dragonlance punches through dragon-like flesh as it skewers the Speaker. The Speaker doesn’t go without a fight however as a well time point blank shatter spell manages to break apart the lance of Saint George and renders him open towards Morgana’s attacks.

    Thus this is the end to the Speaker’s tale. A sorceress beside him, promising to take care of the airship and crew he leaves behind and finally giving it the proper chance to be more than just a vessel for war, a large hole in his chest letting out blood at an alarming rate, and no raven, fey, mad scientist, or mender in site to bring his spirit back. The Speaker’s eyes go dull and lifeless and his spirit goes straight down.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content: Our story now changes perspective. We shift focus to a ferryman of souls, a changeling with a pseudodragon on his shoulder. Bo Harkness is delivering the soul of a rather unremarkable someone. This soul is on its way to the realm where all those unwanted go, Bo is journeying to Hel. And at the end of the ferryman’s journey, where the soul aboard his carpet departs for the beyond he would see a familiar reptilian figure. Bo would meet yet another person he fought with in Empire City, but on the other side of the veil. A kobold smiles at Bo, a kazoo on one hand and a deck of cards on the other. “Greetings Mr. Harkness, I’m the new Speaker of Hel."

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content:
**Matteo and Despo:**
The inseparable pair of mice continued their work at the café before accepting the offer to be Awakened on April 22, 1779.

However, they did not stay at the café for long after their Awakening. Armed with their wits, their acts, and each other the pair made their way to Broadway. 

The pair did their best as actors among the scene but for all their heart and skill they were often typecast or used solely in narration roles due to their small stature. 

Undeterred from their struggles the pair worked more diligently and became playwrights and directors instead. And while their small size made it difficult for them as performers it became an unlikely asset in their new directions allowing them to give better presentations of what they are looking for during rehearsals and casting. And on more than one occasion dashing across stage to provide an understudy their lines should the actor freeze up during a performance.

As actors they were constantly told they had the gift, but as writers and directors they were able bring their dreams and acts succefully to the stage.

No one is quite sure what happened to the pair however. One day they simply vanished. However, on a rare occasion a new script is delivered, without any author or credentials, and yet these mysterious plays are often great successes for the directors bold enough to try and bring these plays to life.

Matteo and Despo's Bibliography includes:
A nine part series of plays of warrior monks far off in the Astral Sea, a harrowing tale of romance, betrayal, the strength of ones will, and a mysterious Force that flows through all things.

A three act play telling the tale of an cursed piece of jewelry and a group of heroes questing to destroy it, having many hardships and separations along the way.

A series of plays about a local legend, some titanic dinosaur that both causes destruction to the city, but also protects it from other titans.

A play about a minstrel that lives in the sewers that strikes ever couple decades, and a group of misfits that ends its terror.

And many many more.

thread.name: The Speaker of the Dead`s Epilogue

content: Mictlan

Mictlan does not leave right away. They spend several more weeks in town, helping with the rebuilding efforts as best they can. Drop by the library a few times, scribbling fiercely as if their life depends on it. The time is used getting better at being in their own skin, settling in somewhere in the midst of their feathers and learning the art of a smile. 

At the end of the three weeks, they know they do not belong anymore. Mictlan could, if they really tried, but wanderlust has come with the snow-white feathers and they… they want to see. There are only so many years left in their life, after all, and so many places left in the world. 

Before they leave, Mictlan drops by Ferrytown. They greet the shifter children, smiling in only the way only they know how. Enter the herb shop, singing something high and melodious to the plants in Celestial with an underpinning of something deeper in the throat. It somehow still works.

They leave as suddenly as they entered, with a silver for the ferry and the plants glistening, watered. 

Eρευνα stands empty in the docks, waiting for its next owner. There’s a book hidden under a floorboard in there, words spaced between arcane sigils in a sort of a journal most cannot read. 

The shifter speaks with any they come across as they exit the city, because politeness dictates it. They are happy, but brief, and will not be stayed. 

A feathered silhouette passes through the land, carrying a bag and following the land due north-northeast. Their steps are light along the road, a familiar shape hovering behind Mictlan’s shoulder all eyes and feathers and rings. Just before they leave sight of the city they step forward and *changes* into something with a large wingspan, striking out with joyous beats of their wings. Their cousin-familiar (Aefirael) follows, spinning.
